items.title: Networking: wire ICE peer candidate exchange
items.detail: Milestone 4 ICE-candidate transport. Exchange the remote peer candidate set through a separately typed, signed, fresh presence/group payload with bounded counts, canonical address validation, credentials, generation, expiry, replacement, and teardown. Feed only the candidate/probe orchestrator. Never format an ICE candidate as the authority match-server route and never pass it directly to netStartClient. Close with focused validation plus ordinary peers across real NAT conditions.

items.title: Networking: publish STUN reflexive to peer
items.detail: Milestone 4 STUN candidate transport. Publish each peer own reflexive candidate as a separately typed, signed, fresh candidate record and consume the remote peer record only inside traversal. Distinguish local discovery, remote candidate, and elected authority match-server route at the type boundary. Reject stale, self, malformed, replayed, or identity-mismatched records and prove real-NAT behavior without a probe-to-netStartClient handoff.

items.title: Networking: UPnP map p2p probe ports
items.detail: Milestone 4 UPnP transport lifecycle. Discover, map, renew, replace, and unmap only the explicit sockets required by the candidate/traversal architecture, with bounded lease behavior and interface-change cleanup. Advertise results only as typed signed candidates. The elected authority separately publishes its validated ENet match-server route after listen startup; UPnP discovery or probe success can never synthesize that route.

items.title: Networking: replace kbps placeholder measurement
items.detail:
Passive prior/current-session upload measurement is now production-connected. The client samples cumulative real ENet sent bytes over completed two-second windows, requires 4096 bytes, persists the best fresh lower bound for 30 days, and signs it in presence v4. Remote reports expire after 90 seconds. Group authority uses highest fresh kbps, match initiator on exact/no-data ties, then smallest public handle; TURN consumes the same fresh reports and removes stale/dropped/failed candidates.

Verification: isolated client/updater/tests compile PASS; [t-networking-004] 37 assertions/5 cases; full pd-tests 56,664/1,036; ordinary two-process results-20260812T151813Z.json PASS 23/23 with host/client real-match measurements 64/32 kbps persisted in each isolated pd.ini and clean exits.

Boundary: this item closes the measurement placeholder and its signed election/relay input. Automatic live listen-host migration and the broader P2P-to-ENet endpoint handoff remain T-NETWORKING-008/T-NETWORKING-006.

items.title: Networking: add TURN public relay fallback
items.detail: Milestone 4 relay fallback. Define a configurable authenticated public TURN service, credential rotation, capacity and abuse limits, typed signed relay candidates, expiry, health, teardown, and user-visible failure. A relay descriptor remains candidate/orchestration data, not a match-server route. Complete only when ordinary peers can reach the elected server-authoritative listen match through the relay path with protocol, identity, catalog, and rollback validation intact.

items.title: Networking: unify legacy hole-punch with tier machine
items.detail: Milestone 4 traversal consolidation after candidate semantics are correct. Retire overlapping legacy hole-punch ownership and leave one bounded candidate/probe orchestrator with explicit attempt, timeout, cancellation, replacement, and teardown states. Preserve D-003 as a separate authority route plane: exactly one authority starts its listen host and publishes the typed signed server route; non-authorities perform one idempotent join. Candidate, probe, and relay outputs cannot call netStartClient directly.

items.title: B-350: airborne side-entry through overhead collision blockers
evidence:
Legacy tracker statement: Code/build slice completed 2026-05-19. Root cause: player airborne movement applied horizontal X/Z first, then bwalkUpdateVertical() only swept move=(0, verticalDelta, 0), so side-entry during a jump could bypass the side plane before vertical clamping. Fix: src/game/bondwalk.c adds bwalkClampAirborneSideEntry(), an upward diagonal capsuleSweep() from bondprevpos to the already-applied X/Z plus verticalDelta; on hit it rolls X/Z back to the safe fraction and clamps/kills upward velocity for ceiling-class hits. Test fixture now covers side-wall rendered triangles. Verification passed: scoped git diff --check, b350side tests target, focused [physics][jump] (99 assertions / 4 cases), and b350side all-target build. options.label: Host-local queue (no net message)
options.tradeoff: Queue Match is a host-convenience feature; the host cycles settings as matches end and clients simply load whatever the next match is. Simplest to ship, no protocol change, fits the P3-deferred scope. The queued-count badge is host-screen-only; joined clients cannot see how many matches are queued or what is coming. No SVC_QUEUE_STATE, no protocol bump, no resync-path changes.

options.label: Networked queue (SVC_QUEUE_STATE + protocol bump)
options.tradeoff: Every player sees the queued count and upcoming settings, which suits organized/tournament play and matches the 'badge displays queued count' intent for all participants. Adds a new SVC_QUEUE_STATE message, a NET_PROTOCOL_VER increment (must update g_TestExpectedNetProtocolVer in tests/test_versions.cpp in the same change per the silent-bump guard), queue state in the resync path, and a larger test surface.

Replacement five-path v2 recording/format/reader foundation is source-frozen on canonical fadf9ff6 with the N-0069 shared lifecycle seam connected read-only through game/prop.h. Every recordable prop is keyed by its never-zero process-lifetime allocation generation rather than an address or mutable-state fingerprint. A zero generation rejects the initial checkpoint and deletes the unpublished candidate, or rolls back a later checkpoint and finalizes only the last accepted prefix.

The codec persists typed manifest/config identity, Campaign variant and roster roles, participant views/orientation, semantic checkpoints/events, a deterministic seek index, and atomic .part lifecycle. Clean finish and durable-END header repair publish COMPLETE; an interrupted accepted prefix reconstructed without a durable END publishes COMPLETE|RECOVERED, and validated replay-list state exposes both flags. Full record CRC/header damage and semantic corruption reject without publication.

Route work through five ordered milestones: T-RELEASE-002 base game and graphs, T-RELEASE-003 Theater, T-RELEASE-004 sample weapon, T-RELEASE-005 friend play and performance, then T-RELEASE-006 release-candidate qualification. The two-view frame is a developer tool: it creates no second local player, bindings or UI (the single-local-player constraint stands).

items.title: 2.0 renderer step 2: where the build gets the HLSL compiler for Direct3D 11 shaders

items.title: Movement: land Manager 4's jump and ground-support rewrite, or keep it parked

options.label: Land it after its own tests
options.tradeoff: Fix one committed pin (tests/test_scene_dispatch.cpp:419), build, run [physics][jump] and the four Complex and Villa smokes, then land. Changes what every player stands on (tables, props, lifts, mesh-only floors) and gives simulants a checked landing; nobody has run it yet, and it narrows simulant jumping to Hard and above.

options.label: Land only the test events and fixtures
options.tradeoff: Brings the movement_ledge and movement_tabletop smoke events, their schema entry and four fixtures, which change nothing in play; the solver stays parked.

options.label: Keep it all parked
options.tradeoff: Nothing changes in the game; the work waits in the canonical checkout and on week-pd/inflight-20261120 until a session can run its tests.

items.detail: Manager 4 (codex-8e25800d-a840aeee, T-ENGINE-006) wrote it on 2026-11-18 and Mike paused it before any build: src/game/bot.c, botmgr.c, chr.c, bondwalk.c, bot.h, types.h (aibot fields), src/lib/capsule.c/.h, collision.c, meshcollision.c/.h, tests/test_jump_two_stage_design.cpp, the smoke harness events and four fixtures. It is uncommitted in the canonical checkout. It changes ordinary play: bondwalk.c's support lookup lets a table, prop, lift or rendered floor beat the tile under the player's feet, collision.c clears floor flags when no ground is found, and capsule.c ray-casts the world grid under every capsule sweep. Simulant jumping (Bot Jumping, off by default) gets a swept arc to a checked landing; committed bot.c lets every difficulty jump toward a higher target, citing Mike's directive of 2026-05-17, and the rewrite keeps that for Hard and above only. Against it, tests/test_scene_dispatch.cpp:419 fails (it pins `botLiveChrFromPropnum(chr->aibot->attackpropnum)`, the rewrite writes `aibot->attackpropnum`).

items.title: Release: bundle the Maian Crystal Pistol sample with the release, enabled on a clean profile

options.label: Bundle and enable it
options.tradeoff: The next release packs crystal_pistol.pdmod under mods/bundled and a clean profile enables it on first run, so every player gets a working sample mod; needs the source provenance and BYOR disposition N-1088 asks for, and an updater overwrites an installed copy.

options.label: Ship without it
options.tradeoff: The release packs no mod; the pistol stays a dev mod that normal builds copy into their own install. Nothing more to clear before a release.

evidence: dev commit 4ac5f8c7 (the packaging step, switched off)
items.detail: Manager 2's packaging step is on dev (4ac5f8c7) and does nothing until a dev-mods.json entry has "release": true. The switch, dev-mods/dev-mods.json (crystal_pistol release false to true) and dev-mods/crystal_pistol/mod.json (the name and description lose their 'test' wording), is uncommitted in the canonical checkout. A release cut from that checkout while those two files stay edited bundles the pistol.
